transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

Probably not faulty. Heat-pump dryers work very differently from older condenser/vented models:

• They dry at a much lower temperature, typically around 45–60°C rather than the very hot air of an older dryer.
• They take longer, especially on “Eco” or cotton/towel programmes. A 3–4 hour cycle for a full load of towels can be normal.
• The first 20–30 minutes can feel only mildly warm while the machine stabilises the temperature and starts removing moisture.
• Opening the door during a programme lets humid air in and can interrupt the sensors, so it can extend the run.

Your old dryer doing towels in about 90 minutes is believable, but it was likely using considerably more electricity and higher heat. Heat-pump dryers trade speed for lower energy use and gentler drying.

Things worth checking:

1. Use a high spin speed first – ideally 1,200–1,400 rpm or higher for towels. A dryer has to remove vastly more water from a 1,000-rpm load than a 1,400-rpm one.
2. Choose the right programme – use Cotton/Towels and “Cupboard Dry” or “Extra Dry,” not Iron Dry or a low-energy/low-dryness setting.
3. Don’t overfill it – towels need room to tumble; a tightly packed drum dries slowly.
4. Clean the lint filters after every load. Also clean any lower/condenser filter only as the manufacturer instructs.
5. Check water is being collected or drained. After a damp load, there should normally be water in the tank (unless plumbed into a drain). No water at all may indicate it is not actually extracting moisture.
6. Room temperature matters. Heat-pump dryers are slower in a cold garage or utility room, particularly below roughly 10–15°C.
7. Clean the moisture-sensor strips inside the drum if your model has them. A film from fabric conditioner can make the dryer misread the load; follow the manual’s cleaning advice.

It would be worth contacting the retailer/manufacturer under warranty if, after an hour or so, the drum air is still genuinely cold, the machine never collects/drains water from wet laundry, clothes remain wet at the end of a correctly selected cycle, it shows an error, or drying times are dramatically longer than the manual’s stated figures under normal conditions.

But on the facts given — towels taking roughly 3½ hours and not feeling very hot early on — that is unfortunately quite typical heat-pump-dryer behaviour rather than clear evidence of a fault.
